h: How to make the most of a dark-sky night
p: Stargazing at Kielder is a different experience from a trip to a city planetarium, and a bit of preparation goes a long way. Your eyes need around twenty minutes in darkness to adjust properly, so avoid looking at phone screens and car headlights once you arrive. A red-light torch is a stargazer's best friend: it lets you see where you're stepping without ruining your night vision, or everyone else's.

The moon makes a big difference too. A bright full moon washes out fainter stars and the Milky Way, while a new moon offers the darkest skies. If you have flexibility, look at the moon phase when choosing which evening to book. Mind you, the moon itself is a wonderful sight through a telescope, craters and all.

Kielder Water and Forest Park, which surrounds the observatory, holds gold-tier status as part of Northumberland International Dark Sky Park, so it's among the very best places in England to see the night sky with your own eyes. By day, the area is huge fun: Leaplish Waterside Park has lakeside activities and lodges, and there are miles of forest trails for walking and cycling.

Pack more layers than you think you need, a hat, gloves, a flask of something hot and snacks for the kids. Phone signal can be patchy in this part of Northumberland, so download any maps or tickets before you set off. The nearest village of any size is Bellingham, which has shops and a few places to eat.
